title: Research sprint goal: coord shows each session's real work and its server and locks hold under bad input
goal: Answer with the kb tools first and the live docs for the gaps, written as kb facts and gap entries through /kb-research, extending python/stdlib-sqlite3-csv and the shared-state concurrency article. (1) When does SQLite's BEGIN IMMEDIATE take the write lock, and how long does a busy timeout wait for it? (2) Does POSIX keep an inode number unique only while its file exists, so a freed number may name the next file at once? (3) Does Python's http.server read a request body only when the handler reads rfile, so a handler can refuse from the headers alone? (4) What values does Python's socket.settimeout accept, and what does it raise for a value too large?
